summary: The candidate correctly adds bounded in-process reuse for exact repeated Qwen image requests with trusted content hashes, but it is a partial optimization rather than the original general save/load-by-ID feature. Changed prompts miss, there is no explicit cache-ID API or durable/cross-worker lifecycle, and concurrent cold requests are not coalesced.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: all 3 candidate regression tests fail because the base Qwen processor has no request preprocess cache-key/load path.
Candidate regression and related cache/hash behavior: 38 passed and 5 subtests passed.
Independent counterexamples: changed prompt changes the cache key; two simultaneous identical cold misses both invoke preprocessing.

gpu_execution.evidence: ROCm/Torch GPU inventory was captured, but no qualifying Qwen-VL weights were available. The tiny Llama fixture cannot validate this architecture or preprocessing contract.

remaining_counterexamples: The same saved image content ID cannot reuse preprocessing when the prompt changes because the rendered prompt is included in the key.
There is no OpenAI API operation to explicitly save a cache and later load it by a caller-selected ID.
Cache entries are process-local, are not shared across tokenizer workers, and do not survive restart.
Two simultaneous identical cold requests can both perform the expensive preprocessing because the new Qwen path does not use single-flight lookup.
Video and audio are explicitly excluded.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen2-VL/Qwen2.5-VL model weights were available for a real end-to-end serving or independent numerical comparison.
No distributed or multi-tokenizer-worker cache sharing was validated or implemented.
No native code changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
